bacterial_leaf_blight.description: A serious bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae. Leaves show water-soaked margins that turn yellow and eventually white.
bacterial_leaf_blight.causes: Warm temperatures (25–30°C), high humidity, and typhoon/rain-splash that spreads the bacteria through leaf wounds.
bacterial_leaf_blight.treatment_summary: Apply copper-based bactericides. Remove infected plant debris. Use resistant varieties. Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization.
bacterial_leaf_blight.prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds. Maintain field drainage. Apply balanced fertilization.

brown_spot.description: Fungal disease caused by Cochliobolus miyabeanus. Oval to circular brown lesions with yellow halos appear on leaves.
brown_spot.causes: Associated with nutrient-deficient soils (especially potassium and silicon). Favoured by warm humid conditions and poor soil health.
brown_spot.treatment_summary: Apply mancozeb or iprodione fungicide. Correct soil nutrient deficiencies (potassium, silicon). Reduce dense planting.
brown_spot.prevention: Balanced fertilization, well-drained soils, disease-resistant varieties.

healthy.description: The leaf appears healthy with no visible disease symptoms.
healthy.treatment_summary: Continue regular monitoring and preventive care.
healthy.prevention: Maintain good agronomic practices, balanced fertilization, and proper irrigation.

leaf_blast.description: One of the most destructive rice diseases, caused by Magnaporthe oryzae. Diamond-shaped lesions with grey centres and brown borders appear on leaves.
leaf_blast.causes: Cool nights, warm days, high humidity (>90%), heavy dew, excessive nitrogen application, and susceptible varieties.
leaf_blast.treatment_summary: Apply fungicides: tricyclazole, isoprothiolane, or azoxystrobin. Reduce nitrogen fertilizer. Drain fields to reduce humidity.
leaf_blast.prevention: Use blast-resistant varieties. Avoid excess nitrogen. Ensure good airflow between plants.

leaf_scald.description: Caused by Microdochium oryzae. Alternating light and dark brown bands appear along leaf margins creating a 'zonate' pattern.
leaf_scald.causes: High humidity, warm temperatures, and dense planting that reduces airflow.
leaf_scald.treatment_summary: Apply propiconazole or carbendazim fungicide. Improve field drainage and plant spacing.
leaf_scald.prevention: Wider row spacing, balanced nutrients, resistant varieties.

sheath_blight.description: Caused by Rhizoctonia solani. Oval greenish-grey lesions with dark brown borders appear on leaf sheaths, spreading to leaves.
sheath_blight.causes: High humidity (>90%), temperatures of 28–32°C, dense planting, high nitrogen levels, and flooded conditions that allow mycelium spread.
sheath_blight.treatment_summary: Apply validamycin, hexaconazole, or propiconazole fungicides. Reduce plant density. Minimize canopy humidity.
sheath_blight.prevention: Lower seeding rates, balanced fertilization, water management.

aphid.description: Small soft-bodied insects that cluster on leaves and stems, sucking plant sap and potentially transmitting viruses.
aphid.causes: Warm dry conditions, absence of natural predators, and dense planting.
aphid.treatment_summary: Apply imidacloprid or lambda-cyhalothrin insecticide. Encourage natural predators (ladybugs).
aphid.prevention: Early planting, crop rotation, avoid excessive nitrogen.

black_rust.description: Caused by Puccinia graminis. Produces brick-red to black pustules on stems and leaves. Can devastate entire crops.
black_rust.causes: Warm temperatures (15–30°C), dew, and wind-blown spores from nearby infected fields.
black_rust.treatment_summary: Apply propiconazole, tebuconazole, or trifloxystrobin fungicides at early stages.
black_rust.prevention: Plant resistant varieties. Early sowing. Remove volunteer wheat plants.

blast.description: Magnaporthe oryzae. Diamond-shaped lesions on leaves. Can also affect panicles (panicle blast).
blast.causes: Cool nights, morning dew, excess nitrogen, susceptible varieties.
blast.prevention: Resistant varieties, balanced nitrogen, regulated irrigation.

brown_rust.description: Caused by Puccinia triticina. Orange-brown pustules on upper leaf surface. Very common and widespread.
brown_rust.causes: Moderate temperatures (15–22°C), dew, and humid conditions.
brown_rust.treatment_summary: Fungicides: propiconazole, mancozeb. Apply at early infection stage.
brown_rust.prevention: Resistant varieties, timely sowing, crop rotation.

common_root_rot.description: Caused by Bipolaris sorokiniana. Brown to black discolouration of crown and root tissues.
common_root_rot.causes: Dry soil conditions, warm temperatures during seeding, and soil-borne inoculum.
common_root_rot.treatment_summary: Seed treatment with trifloxystrobin + tebuconazole. Crop rotation with non-cereal crops.
common_root_rot.prevention: Balanced soil fertility, avoid continuous wheat, proper seeding depth.

fusarium_head_blight.description: Caused by Fusarium graminearum. Bleached spikelets with pink mold. Produces mycotoxins (DON) that contaminate grain.
fusarium_head_blight.causes: Wet conditions during flowering (anthesis), temperatures of 25–30°C, and crop residues.
fusarium_head_blight.treatment_summary: Apply thiophanate-methyl or metconazole at early flowering. Remove infected debris.
fusarium_head_blight.prevention: Resistant varieties, tillage to bury residues, good drainage.

leaf_blight.description: Tan-brown lesions with yellow borders on older leaves.
leaf_blight.causes: Warm humid conditions and susceptible varieties.
leaf_blight.prevention: Crop rotation and use of resistant varieties.

mildew.description: White powdery coating on leaves, caused by Blumeria graminis. Reduces photosynthesis.
mildew.causes: Cool temperatures (15–22°C), moderate humidity, and dense canopy.
mildew.treatment_summary: Apply triadimefon, propiconazole, or sulfur-based fungicides.
mildew.prevention: Wider row spacing, resistant varieties, early sowing.

mite.description: Tiny arachnids causing silvery stippling and bronzing of leaves.
mite.causes: Hot, dry conditions. Chemical treatments that kill natural predators.
mite.treatment_summary: Apply abamectin or dicofol miticide. Increase irrigation.
mite.prevention: Avoid overly dry conditions. Conserve beneficial insects.

septoria.description: Caused by Zymoseptoria tritici. Pale green-yellow blotches with brown necrosis and pycnidia on leaves.
septoria.causes: Cool, wet weather (10–20°C), leaf wetness periods >20 hours.
septoria.treatment_summary: Triazole or SDHI fungicides (epoxiconazole, fluxapyroxad). Early application is key.
septoria.prevention: Resistant varieties, crop rotation, delayed sowing.

smut.description: Caused by Ustilago tritici. Spikes replaced by black powdery masses of teliospores.
smut.causes: Moderate temperatures during flowering with humid conditions. Seed-borne pathogen.
smut.treatment_summary: Seed treatment with carboxin, thiram, or tebuconazole is highly effective.
smut.prevention: Use certified smut-free seed. Hot-water seed treatment.

stem_fly.description: Larval mining inside wheat stems causing 'dead heart' symptoms in young plants.
stem_fly.causes: Peak activity during cool temperatures (15–20°C) at early crop stages.
stem_fly.treatment_summary: Apply chlorpyrifos or imidacloprid at seedling stage.
stem_fly.prevention: Early sowing, treat seeds with systemic insecticide, monitor basal nodes.

tan_spot.description: Caused by Pyrenophora tritici-repentis. Tan-colored oval lesions with yellow borders.
tan_spot.causes: Warm temperatures (20–28°C), leaf wetness, and crop residue from previous season.
tan_spot.treatment_summary: Apply propiconazole or mancozeb. Tillage to bury residues.
tan_spot.prevention: Crop rotation, residue management, resistant varieties.

yellow_rust.description: Caused by Puccinia striiformis. Bright yellow pustules in stripes along leaf veins. Very destructive in cool climates.
yellow_rust.causes: Cool temperatures (10–15°C), dew and mist, and susceptible varieties.
yellow_rust.treatment_summary: Apply propiconazole, tebuconazole, or other triazole fungicides early.
yellow_rust.prevention: Resistant varieties are most effective. Early sowing. Monitor forecasts.

mosaic_disease.description: Caused by Sugarcane Mosaic Virus (SCMV). Mosaic or mottled discolouration of leaves — alternating light and dark green patches.
mosaic_disease.causes: Transmitted by aphids (Rhopalosiphum maidis), infected planting material.
mosaic_disease.treatment_summary: No chemical cure. Remove and destroy infected stools. Control aphid vectors.
mosaic_disease.prevention: Use virus-free seed cane, resistant varieties, control aphid populations.

rust.description: Caused by Puccinia melanocephala. Orange-brown pustules on leaf undersides causing premature leaf death.
rust.causes: Warm temperatures (24–28°C), high humidity, and susceptible cultivars.
rust.treatment_summary: Apply triadimefon or propiconazole fungicide. Remove severely infected leaves.

bacterial_blight.description: Caused by Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. malvacearum. Angular water-soaked lesions on leaves, black cankers on stems.
bacterial_blight.causes: Warm, humid weather, rain-splash, mechanical damage, and infected seeds.
bacterial_blight.treatment_summary: Apply copper oxychloride or streptomycin spray. Remove infected debris.
bacterial_blight.prevention: Disease-free certified seed, seed treatment, crop rotation.

alternaria_leaf_spot.description: Caused by Alternaria macrospora. Dark brown to black circular spots with concentric rings on leaves.
alternaria_leaf_spot.causes: High humidity and temperatures of 25–30°C. Most severe on stressed or weakened plants.
alternaria_leaf_spot.treatment_summary: Apply mancozeb, chlorothalonil, or iprodione fungicide.
alternaria_leaf_spot.prevention: Good drainage, balanced nutrition, remove infected debris.

hispa.description: Caused by Dicladispa armigera (leaf beetle). Adults scrape leaf surfaces; larvae mine inside leaves creating white tunnels.
hispa.causes: Lush, dense crops with high nitrogen. Wet season conditions.
hispa.treatment_summary: Apply malathion or monocrotophos. Clip and destroy affected leaves.
hispa.prevention: Avoid over-fertilization, resistant varieties, reduce dense planting.

tungro.description: Caused by two viruses (RTBV + RTSV) transmitted by green leafhoppers. Leaves turn yellow-orange. Stunted plants with reduced tillering.
tungro.causes: Green leafhopper (Nephotettix spp.) populations carrying both viruses.
tungro.treatment_summary: No direct cure. Control leafhopper vectors with buprofezin or imidacloprid.
tungro.prevention: Resistant varieties (Utri Merah), synchronized planting, leafhopper management.

dead_heart.description: Caused by stem borer larvae (Scirpophaga incertulas). The central leaf whorl turns yellow and dies — pulled out easily.
dead_heart.causes: Stem borer moth populations during vegetative stage.
dead_heart.treatment_summary: Apply cartap hydrochloride, chlorpyrifos, or flubendiamide granules.
dead_heart.prevention: Avoid early planting when moths are active. Use light traps. Remove egg masses.

downy_mildew.description: Caused by Sclerophthora macrospora. Pale yellow lesions with downy growth on underside of leaves.
downy_mildew.causes: Waterlogged soils, cool temperatures, and high humidity.
downy_mildew.treatment_summary: Apply metalaxyl or fosetyl-aluminium fungicide. Improve drainage.
downy_mildew.prevention: Avoid water stagnation, improve field drainage, resistant varieties.

bacterial_leaf_streak.description: Caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzicola. Narrow, translucent water-soaked stripes between veins.
bacterial_leaf_streak.causes: Warm, humid weather. Spread by rain splash and irrigation water.
bacterial_leaf_streak.treatment_summary: Apply copper-based bactericides. Remove infected leaves.
bacterial_leaf_streak.prevention: Use resistant varieties. Avoid excessive nitrogen.

bacterial_panicle_blight.description: Caused by Burkholderia glumae. Sterile spikelets, grayish-brown discolouration. Significant yield loss.
bacterial_panicle_blight.causes: High temperatures (>30°C) during flowering combined with high humidity.
bacterial_panicle_blight.treatment_summary: Apply oxolinic acid or copper-based bactericide at panicle initiation.
bacterial_panicle_blight.prevention: Resistant varieties, avoid water stress at heading.

normal.description: No disease detected. Crop appears healthy.
normal.treatment_summary: Continue routine monitoring and preventive agronomic practices.
normal.prevention: Maintain balanced fertilization, proper irrigation, and crop rotation.
